initial.name: adcs_find
initial.description: Collect Active Directory Certificate Services configuration from one authorized assessment domain with an authenticated account (certipy find -stdout) and return certificate-authority and template rows. `-vulnerable` restricts the report to entries with known escalation paths (ESC classes). The domain must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant and the credential reference must be granted; this is read-only directory collection, not exploitation.

target_id.description: Domain to collect ADCS configuration from, as declared in the assessment scope grant (e.g. lab.example.invalid).

username.description: Authenticated account name whose granted credential performs the collection.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_AD_PASS). The value never enters the conversation.

vulnerable_only.description: Report only certificate authorities and templates with known escalation paths (-vulnerable).

initial.name: aliyun_identity_get
initial.description: Confirm which Alibaba Cloud identity the granted credentials resolve to (aliyun sts GetCallerIdentity) and return the identity type, account id, and ARN. The target_id must match a cloud target declared in the active assessment-scope grant and the credential reference must be granted; this is a read-only identity confirmation, not enumeration.

target_id.description: Alibaba Cloud account id to confirm access to, as declared in the assessment scope grant.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_ALIYUN_KEYS). The value never enters the conversation.

region.description: Explicit Alibaba Cloud region for --region; must fall inside the region allowlist of the matched cloud target. RAM is a global product: use the account's center region.

initial.name: asrep_roast
initial.description: Request pre-authentication data for accounts without Kerberos pre-authentication in one authorized assessment domain (impacket GetNPUsers) and return hashcat-format AS-REP Roasting hash rows with account names for offline cracking. The domain must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant and the credential reference must be granted for that target.

target_id.description: Domain to enumerate no-pre-auth accounts for, as declared in the assessment scope grant.

username.description: Authenticated account name whose granted credential performs the enumeration.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret. The value never enters the conversation.

dc_ip.description: Domain controller address for -dc-ip when the domain needs explicit routing.

initial.name: az_account_show
initial.description: Confirm which Azure subscriptions the granted service principal can reach (az login --service-principal) and return the subscription rows with tenant ids. The target_id must match a cloud target declared in the active assessment-scope grant and the credential reference must be granted; this is a read-only identity confirmation, not enumeration.

target_id.description: Azure tenant or account id to confirm access to, as declared in the assessment scope grant.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_AZURE_SP). The value never enters the conversation.

initial.name: azure_ad_enum
initial.description: Enumerate one authorized Azure tenant through the granted service principal (az ad user list or az role assignment list) and return bounded rows. The target_id must match a cloud target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; this is read-only Entra reconnaissance, not exploitation.

target_id.description: Azure tenant or account id to enumerate, as declared in the assessment scope grant.

resource.description: Entra collection to list: directory users or role assignments.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_AZURE_SP). The value never enters the conversation.

subscription.description: Azure subscription GUID to scope the call via --subscription; must fall inside the subscription allowlist of the matched cloud target.

initial.name: azure_storage_enum
initial.description: List the storage accounts of the granted Azure service principal (az storage account list) and return rows with each account's blob-public-access and HTTPS-only settings. The target_id must match a cloud target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; this is read-only storage reconnaissance.

target_id.description: Azure tenant or account id to enumerate, as declared in the assessment scope grant.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_AZURE_SP). The value never enters the conversation.

subscription.description: Azure subscription GUID to scope the call via --subscription; must fall inside the subscription allowlist of the matched cloud target.

initial.name: bloodhound_enum
initial.description: Collect directory data from one authorized assessment domain with an authenticated account (bloodhound-python -c All) and return a triage summary: per-collector row counts plus the Kerberoastable and AS-REP Roastable account lists extracted from users.json. The domain must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant and the credential reference must be granted for that target; collection is read-only directory enumeration, not exploitation. Raw collector JSON stays in a temporary directory that is removed after aggregation.

target_id.description: Domain to collect from, as declared in the assessment scope grant (e.g. lab.example.invalid).

username.description: Authenticated account name whose granted credential performs the collection.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_AD_PASS). The value never enters the conversation.

nameserver.description: Domain controller address used as the -ns nameserver to resolve the domain.

resource.description: CAM collection to list: users or roles.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_TENCENT_KEYS). The value never enters the conversation. Optional: without it the local tccli configuration chain supplies the credentials.

Verify the grant with cam_policy_detach afterwards.

Detaching a policy that is not attached fails with a clear CLI error.

target_id.description: Tencent Cloud account id holding the user and policy, as declared in the assessment scope grant.

policy_id.description: Numeric id of an existing CAM policy; no policy document is ever composed.

uin.description: Numeric UIN of the CAM user the policy is granted to or rolled back for.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_TENCENT_KEYS). The value never enters the conversation. Optional: without it the local tccli configuration chain supplies the credentials.

initial.name: cos_enum
initial.description: List the COS buckets of one authorized Tencent Cloud account through the granted credentials (tccli cos GetService) and optionally check each bucket's ACL for anonymous-read grants with GetBucketAcl. The target_id must match a cloud target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; this is read-only storage reconnaissance.

region.description: Explicit Tencent Cloud region for --region; must fall inside the region allowlist of the matched cloud target.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.name: edit
initial.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: ffuf_fuzz
initial.description: Fuzz one authorized assessment target URL with ffuf and a local wordlist: directory/file discovery, parameter names, or header values depending on where the FUZZ keyword sits. Returns structured match rows (keyword, URL, status, length). The URL host must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; out-of-scope URLs are denied before execution. Rate is left at ffuf defaults — no aggressive fuzzing flags are emitted.

url.description: Target URL containing the literal FUZZ keyword where wordlist entries are substituted, e.g. https://target.example.com/FUZZ or https://target.example.com/search?q=FUZZ.

wordlist.description: Absolute or relative wordlist file path on the execution host (-w).

method.description: HTTP method (-X), e.g. POST. Defaults to GET.

matchCodes.description: Whitespace/comma-separated status codes to keep (-mc), e.g. 200,301,403.

autoCalibrate.description: Auto-filter noise responses (-ac). Defaults to true.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-request timeout in seconds (-timeout). Defaults to ffuf's 10.

initial.name: gau_urls
initial.description: Fetch known URLs for one authorized assessment target domain from passive historical data sources (wayback, commoncrawl, otx, urlscan) and return deduplicated URL rows. This tool never contacts the target domain itself — all queries go to third-party archives. The domain must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; out-of-scope domains are denied before execution.

target_id.description: Root domain as declared in the assessment scope grant (e.g. example.invalid).

providers.description: Restrict the passive sources (--providers) to a subset of wayback, commoncrawl, otx, urlscan. Omit to use the tool default of all sources.

The target_id must match a cloud target declared in the active assessment-scope grant and the project must fall inside the target allowlist; this is read-only IAM reconnaissance, not exploitation.

target_id.description: GCP account to enumerate, as declared in the assessment scope grant.

project.description: GCP project id; must fall inside the project allowlist of the matched cloud target.

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted service-account JSON. The value never enters the conversation.

initial.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

initial.name: glob
initial.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

initial.name: grep
initial.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

initial.name: httpx_probe
initial.description: Probe authorized assessment targets for live HTTP/HTTPS services and return structured rows: URL, status code, title, technologies, web server, and CDN. Each target must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; out-of-scope targets are denied before execution. This is reconnaissance only — no injection, fuzzing, or exploitation payloads are sent.

target_id.description: Whitespace/comma-separated probe targets as declared in the assessment scope grant: hostnames, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, URLs, or CIDR ranges (at most 1000).

statusCode.description: Include the HTTP status code (-status-code). Defaults to false.

title.description: Extract the page title (-title). Defaults to false.

techDetect.description: Report detected technologies (-tech-detect). Defaults to false.

https.description: Probe https:// scheme (-no-https when false). Defaults to true.

http.description: Probe http:// scheme (-no-http when false). Defaults to true.

initial.name: interrupt_agent
initial.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

initial.name: job_kill
initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

initial.name: job_list
initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output
initial.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

initial.name: naabu_scan
initial.description: Run a naabu fast TCP port scan against authorized assessment targets and return structured open-port rows (host, IP, port). Discovers open ports only — no service fingerprinting, vulnerability probing, or payload delivery. Each target must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; out-of-scope targets are denied before execution. SYN scanning requires elevated privileges on most platforms.

target_id.description: Whitespace/comma-separated scan targets as declared in the assessment scope grant: hostnames, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, or CIDR ranges (at most 1000).

ports.description: Port specification for -p: digits, commas, hyphens (e.g. 22,80,443 or 1-1000). Required unless topPorts is given.

topPorts.description: Scan the N most common ports (-top-ports). Mutually exclusive with ports.

initial.name: nmap_scan
initial.description: Run an nmap port scan against one authorized assessment target and return structured host/port/service results parsed from XML output. The target must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; out-of-scope targets are denied before execution. No vulnerability scripts are run — this is reconnaissance only.

target_id.description: Scan target as declared in the assessment scope grant: hostname, IPv4/IPv6 address, or CIDR range (e.g. 192.0.2.10, scanme.nmap.org, 10.0.0.0/24).

ports.description: Port specification for -p: digits, commas, hyphens (e.g. 22,80,443 or 1-1024). Mutually exclusive with topPorts.

topPorts.description: Scan the N most common ports (--top-ports). Mutually exclusive with ports.

serviceDetection.description: Enable -sV service/version detection (slower, more accurate service names).

osDetection.description: Enable -O OS fingerprinting. Requires elevated privileges on most platforms.

openOnly.description: Report only open ports (--open). Defaults to true.

timing.description: nmap timing template -T0 (paranoid) through -T5 (insane). Defaults to nmap's -T3.

initial.name: ntlm_relay
initial.description: Bind local SMB/HTTP listeners and relay captured authentication to one authorized assessment target with ntlmrelayx as a background job. The call returns a job id at once; read relayed-authentication events with job_output and stop the session with job_kill. The relay target is the run's only outbound destination and must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; this is exploit execution, so each call typically requires approval.

target_id.description: Relay target host, as declared in the assessment scope grant (the destination for captured authentication).

scheme.description: Relay target scheme (-t): smb (default), http, or ldaps.

listen_window_ms.description: Listen window in milliseconds; the deployment maxListenMs caps the accepted value.

initial.name: nuclei_scan
initial.description: Run nuclei template-based vulnerability checks against authorized assessment targets and return structured finding rows (template, severity, matched URL). Template selection and severity filtering are exposed; DAST/exploit-grade flags and out-of-band callbacks are disabled by default. Each target must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant; out-of-scope targets are denied before execution.

target_id.description: Whitespace/comma-separated scan targets as declared in the assessment scope grant: URLs or bare hosts (at most 100).

templates.description: Whitespace/comma-separated template IDs or local template paths (-t). Omit to run the default template set.

severities.description: Whitespace/comma-separated severity filter (-severity): info, low, medium, high, critical.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-request timeout in seconds (-timeout). Defaults to nuclei's 10.

initial.name: nxc_spray
initial.description: Try one granted credential against candidate accounts on one authorized assessment host with nxc (NetExec) and return structured hit rows with the secret scrubbed. The host must match a target declared in the active assessment-scope grant and the credential reference must be granted for that target; the thread count is bounded by deployment config. This is credential validation, not exploitation.

usernames.description: Candidate account names to try with the granted secret (1-100 entries).

credential_ref.description: Environment-variable-shaped name of the granted credential secret (e.g. ASSESS_AD_PASS). The value never enters the conversation.

protocol.description: Protocol subcommand: smb (default), ldap, mssql, winrm, or ssh.

domain.description: Fully-qualified domain for domain-qualified authentication attempts (-d).

threads.description: Parallel workers (--threads). The deployment-configured cap (maxThreads) limits the accepted value.

initial.name: pwsh
initial.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: ralph
initial.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

initial.name: subagent

The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.
